# kryptos 🔐

![kryptos](https://img.shields.io/badge/secrets--SSOT-7A28A0?style=for-the-badge) ![bun](https://img.shields.io/badge/runtime-bun-F9E000?style=for-the-badge&logo=bun&logoColor=black) ![freedesktop](https://img.shields.io/badge/Secret%20Service-181717?style=for-the-badge)

> **kryptos** (Greek: κρυπτός, "hidden") — the secrets SSOT for the estate:
> a from-scratch [freedesktop Secret Service][ss] CLI + the **keypool** router
> that races provider keys with per-key health, cooldowns and quota lanes.
>
> [ss]: https://specifications.freedesktop.org/secret-service/latest/

```bash
secretsmith set MY_KEY                 # store into the Default keyring
secretsmith get MY_KEY                 # read (secrets print by default)
secretsmith get MY_KEY --redact        # mask for share/screenshot surfaces
secretsmith env --app myapp            # export app-scoped env block
secretsmith exec -- cmd args...        # run with secrets injected
secretsmith tau-auth-sync              # mirror tau auth state
```

> Full agent-facing usage, failure shapes, and the 2026-11-02 default-flip
> rationale: [`estate/docs/secretsmith-guide.md`](../../../estate/docs/secretsmith-guide.md)

## What's inside

| Component | What it does |
|---|---|
| `secretsmith.ts` | The Secret Service CLI — D-Bus native via `dbus-next`; schema registry, JSON scripting mode, Chromium `os_crypt` pipeline that can never print the raw key |
| `keypool/` | Provider key-pool router (Bun.serve, :25109): races keys per pool, parks 401s with cooldowns, gap-fills secrets from the keyring SSOT, health probes via event-driven poller |
| `schemas.json` | Schema registry for structured secrets |
| `bin/secretsmith` | Launcher (bin contract: `~/.local/bin/secretsmith → here`) |

## Keypool pools

`openrouter-free`, `openrouter-paid`, `gemini-eap`, `gemini-eap-interactions`,
`nvidia`, … — pool definitions are data, not code: see the estate
`config/keypools.yaml`. Auth headers resolve through one function
(`upstreamAuthHeader`) so a new upstream cannot be half-wired: bearer for
`/openai` lanes, `x-goog-api-key` for Google-native lanes.

## Why kryptos is the master

- Single repo (`toxicwind/kryptos`) — vendored copies in `ranch` and `barn`
  were retired 2026-10-28 (md5-divergence audited, newest code cherry-picked here)
- Label-scoped `--replace`, `exec/env` + alias-map autoload (2026-10-24+)
- Keyring-SSOT secret loading; strict TS typing; TDD quotes contract (41/41)

## Lineage

From-scratch reimplementation of GNOME `secret-tool`'s D-Bus semantics — no
libsecret code. Fork lineage documented for provenance: [GNOME/libsecret](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libsecret).

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

## Secrets SSOT layout

- **Keyring** (D-Bus Secret Service, `Default Keyring`) = the SSOT. `secretsmith env --app <name>` injects an app's keys (matches `service` attribute OR `<APP>_*` label prefix — anomaly #16 contract).
- **keypool** keys are stamped `service=keypool` (12 items: OPENROUTER_*, GEMINI_EAP_KEY*, FREEINFERENCE_API_KEY, MISTRAL_API_KEY) — stanza runs `eval $(secretsmith env --app keypool)`.
- **Recovery vault** `/home/toxic/estate-secrets-recovery/` = post-archive cherry-pick of irreplaceable keys (CA, phone, PGP, graveyard). Not tracked in git (push-protection enforced 2026-10-28).
- **`~/.secrets`** = retired fallback record; keyring gap-fill overrides it (loadSecrets: env → file → keyring).

# cyoa-router — Choose-Your-Own-Adventure weighted router skill

A router where EVERY answer carries a weight that DIFFS the route graph. Orthogonal axes: each question is an independent dimension; the selected option's weight vector is added to the route state; the resolved route is the highest-weighted compatible route.

## Q-bank (12 orthogonal questions)

| # | Question | Options (weight → route effect) |
|---|----------|---------------------------------|
| Q1 | Latency vs quality when they conflict? | A) Latency absolutist → w_speed+3 (2s breach → race faster pattern, always) · B) Quality floor → w_quality+3 (never ship below full verification) · C) Pareto router → w_both+2 (pick from frontier per task shape) |
| Q2 | Autonomy ceiling when plausible-but-unverified? | A) Act-first → w_act+3 (default informed action, escalate only on deadlock) · B) Confirm-at-risk → w_confirm+3 (pause at every consequential edge) · C) Risk-tiered → w_tiered+2 (act freely below irreversible, confirm above) |
| Q3 | Failure posture when a daemon stops cleanly? | A) Fix-forward → w_ff+3 (root-cause + restart, never roll back) · B) Rollback → w_rb+3 (revert to known-good, investigate later) · C) Piecemeal → w_piece+2 (cherry-pick or maximally refactor the broken piece) |
| Q4 | Secrets/keys handling? | A) Vault-first → w_vault+3 (everything through keyring SSOT/secretsmith) · B) Speed → w_speed+3 (raw env vars, fastest path) · C) Hybrid → w_hyb+2 (vault for production, env for sessions) |
| Q5 | Provider/model preference when a free tier is available? | A) Free tier → w_free+3 (prefer free regardless of capability) · B) Instruction-following → w_instr+3 (prefer best instruction-following model) · C) Router-weighted → w_router+2 (router weights: FREE > FAST > follow) |
| Q6 | Concurrency/subagents appetite? | A) High parallelism → w_sub+3 (spawn many subagents, race paths) · B) Serial → w_ser+3 (one turn at a time, deterministic) · C) Adaptive → w_ad+2 (batch independent steps, serialize dependent) |
| Q7 | Git history discipline? | A) Forward-only → w_fwd+3 (dirty tree = git add *, never roll back) · B) Preserve history → w_hist+3 (keep provenance, cherry-pick only) · C) Rewrite → w_rewrite+2 (squash/rebase for clean narrative) |
| Q8 | Verification depth before declaring done? | A) Probe-everything → w_probe+3 (live HTTP + listener + state per change) · B) Smoke test → w_smoke+2 (healthz + one representative case) · C) Code-read → w_read+1 (read + reason, minimal execution) |
| Q9 | Fleet collaboration model? | A) Fleet-debate → w_fleet+3 (ambiguous → squawk fleet debate, architect only on deadlock) · B) Ask-architect → w_arch+3 (halt and ask the architect) · C) Solo-decide → w_solo+2 (decide locally, document after) |
| Q10 | Hardware/latency awareness? | A) NVMe-lane-max → w_nvme+3 (per-NVMe placement, parallel sweeps, same-fs mv) · B) Standard → w_std+2 (uniform treatment) · C) Oblivious → w_obl+1 (ignore hardware) |
| Q11 | Documentation doctrine? | A) Retro-always → w_retro+3 (dossier + KB + AGENTS table every session) · B) Code-only → w_code+2 (docs lie, code is absolute) · C) Contracts-only → w_contract+2 (only capability-contract docs persist) |
| Q12 | Public/star-readiness polish? | A) Star-whore max → w_polish+3 (badges, LICENSE, topics, tags — public-ready) · B) Private utility → w_private+2 (works-for-me beats pretty) · C) Ship-then-shine → w_ship+2 (function first, polish pass later) |

## Routing semantics

- Start state: zero vector over all weights.
- Each answer adds its option's weight vector.
- Route resolution: select the route whose requirement vector has maximal dot product with the accumulated weight vector, subject to route feasibility (daemon healthy, port free, config present).
- Each Q's three options form a simplex: exactly one may be chosen per question; weights are additive across questions.
- The router rejects routes whose constraints contradict the accumulated vector (e.g., w_code-only route cannot be selected if w_retro > w_code).

## Implementation plan (T5 TDD)

1. Write skill/core.ts: `Router` class with `ask(qId, optId)` → `weights: Map<string,number>` and `resolve(routes: Route[]) → Route`.
2. TDD: `test/weight.test.ts` — weight accumulation correctness; `test/route.test.ts` — route selection & contradiction rejection.
3. Golden-path walkthrough: one full quiz run end-to-end → recorded in `test/golden.md`.
4. Wire into `~/.tau/skills/cyoa-router/` (tau skills dir) for fleet use.

## Router contract

- `ask(qId: string, optId: string): void` — record one answer (may be called 12 times, once per question).
- `resolve(routes: Route[]): Route | null` — compute weight vector, filter feasible routes, return max dot product.
- Routes carry `weightReqs: Map<string,number>` (min weights required) and `weightExcludes: Set<string>` (weights that disqualify).

"""Fuzzy-label fallback: `get --label X` finds items when the exact label
misses (case / separator / suffix tolerant). Main-feature contract test."""
import json
import subprocess


def run(*args):
    return subprocess.run(
        ["secretsmith", *args], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60
    )


def test_fuzzy_get_case_insensitive():
    """Lowercased label resolves to the canonical keyring item."""
    r = run("get", "--label", "openrouter_api_key_1", "--show", "--json")
    assert r.returncode == 0, r.stderr
    data = json.loads(r.stdout)
    assert data["label"] == "OPENROUTER_API_KEY_1"
    assert data["secret"]


def test_fuzzy_get_separator_insensitive():
    """Dashes instead of underscores still resolve."""
    r = run("get", "--label", "OPENROUTER-API-KEY-1", "--show", "--json")
    assert r.returncode == 0, r.stderr
    data = json.loads(r.stdout)
    assert data["label"] == "OPENROUTER_API_KEY_1"


def test_fuzzy_get_substring():
    """Partial label (distinct enough) resolves via substring fallback."""
    r = run("get", "--label", "openrouter", "--show", "--json")
    assert r.returncode == 0, r.stderr
    data = json.loads(r.stdout)
    assert data["label"].startswith("OPENROUTER")


def test_fuzzy_get_no_match_errors():
    """Gibberish label still fails cleanly."""
    r = run("get", "--label", "zzz_no_such_secret_zzz", "--show", "--json")
    assert r.returncode != 0


def test_fuzzy_disabled_flag():
    """--no-fuzzy restores strict exact-label behavior."""
    r = run("get", "--label", "openrouter_api_key_1", "--no-fuzzy", "--show", "--json")
    assert r.returncode != 0

class TestRegistry(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_registry_loads(self):
        reg = ssm.load_registry()
        self.assertIn("chromium", reg["schemas"])

    def test_chromium_resolves(self):
        reg = ssm.load_registry()
        schema, entry = ssm.resolve_schema("chromium", reg)
        self.assertEqual(schema, "chrome_libsecret_os_crypt_password_v2")
        self.assertTrue(entry["secret_is_key"])

    def test_chrome_alias(self):
        reg = ssm.load_registry()
        schema, _ = ssm.resolve_schema("chrome", reg)
        self.assertEqual(schema, "chrome_libsecret_os_crypt_password_v2")

    def test_generic_is_not_chromium(self):
        reg = ssm.load_registry()
        schema, _ = ssm.resolve_schema("generic", reg)
        self.assertNotEqual(schema, "chrome_libsecret_os_crypt_password_v2")

    def test_raw_passthrough(self):
        reg = ssm.load_registry()
        schema, entry = ssm.resolve_schema("com.example.Custom", reg)
        self.assertEqual(schema, "com.example.Custom")
        self.assertIn("unregistered", entry["description"])


class TestChromiumCrypto(unittest.TestCase):
    def _blob(self, key, pt):
        from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.ciphers import Cipher, algorithms, modes
        pad = 16 - len(pt) % 16
        pt = pt + bytes([pad]) * pad
        d = Cipher(algorithms.AES(key), modes.CBC(b" " * 16)).encryptor()
        return b"v10" + d.update(pt) + d.finalize()

    def test_roundtrip_raw_key(self):
        key = os.urandom(16)
        blob = self._blob(key, b"hunter2")
        self.assertEqual(ssm.decrypt_chromium_blob(blob, [key]), b"hunter2")

    def test_roundtrip_b64_key(self):
        key = os.urandom(16)
        stored = base64.b64encode(key)  # 24 chars, like the real keyring entry
        self.assertEqual(len(stored), 24)
        blob = self._blob(key, b"correct horse")
        cands = ssm._key_candidates(stored)
        self.assertIn(key, cands)
        self.assertEqual(ssm.decrypt_chromium_blob(blob, cands), b"correct horse")

    def test_wrong_key_fails(self):
        blob = self._blob(os.urandom(16), b"nope")
        with self.assertRaises(ssm.SecretsmithError):
            ssm.decrypt_chromium_blob(blob, [os.urandom(16)])

    def test_bad_prefix_fails(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ssm.SecretsmithError):
            ssm.decrypt_chromium_blob(b"v99" + b"x" * 32, [os.urandom(16)])


class TestSafety(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_redact_format(self):
        self.assertEqual(ssm.redact(24), "<redacted: 24 bytes>")

    def test_parse_attrs(self):
        self.assertEqual(ssm.parse_attrs(["a=1", "b=x=y"]), {"a": "1", "b": "x=y"})

    def test_parse_attrs_rejects_bare(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ssm.SecretsmithError):
            ssm.parse_attrs(["bare"])


class _FakeSvc:
    """In-memory stub of SecretService for the env-loader unit test."""

    def __init__(self, items):
        self._items = items

    def search(self, filters, collection=None, label=None):
        out = []
        for it in self._items:
            # Handle "label" in filters by checking item["label"] not attributes
            eff = {k: v for k, v in filters.items() if k != "label"}
            if not all(it["attributes"].get(k) == v for k, v in eff.items()):
                continue
            if label is not None and it.get("label") != label:
                continue
            out.append(it)
        return out

    def ensure_unlocked_items(self, items):
        return

    def get_secret(self, item_path):
        for it in self._items:
            if it["path"] == item_path:
                return it["_secret"], "text/plain"
        raise ssm.SecretsmithError("no such item")


def _fake_item(label, secret, attrs=None):
    return {
        "label": label,
        "path": "/x/" + label,
        "locked": False,
        "attributes": attrs or {},
        "_secret": secret,
    }


def _env_args(app="", attr=(), as_json=False):

    a = types.SimpleNamespace(app=app, attr=list(attr), collection=None)
    return a, as_json


class TestEnvLoader(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_app_filters_on_service_and_emits_exports(self):
        a, as_json = _env_args(app="kappa")
        svc = _FakeSvc([
            _fake_item("KAPPA_SERVER_PASSWORD", b"s3cr3t", {"service": "kappa"}),
            _fake_item("OTHER", b"x", {"service": "else"}),
        ])
        with _capture_stdout() as out:
            rc = ssm.cmd_env(svc, a, ssm.load_registry(), as_json)
        text = out.getvalue()
        self.assertEqual(rc, 0)
        self.assertIn("KAPPA_SERVER_PASSWORD='s3cr3t'", text)
        self.assertNotIn("OTHER", text)
        self.assertNotIn("else", text)

    def test_invalid_identifier_label_skipped(self):
        a, as_json = _env_args(app="kappa")
        svc = _FakeSvc([
            _fake_item("kappa-freeinference", b"x", {"service": "kappa"}),
        ])
        with _capture_stdout() as out:
            rc = ssm.cmd_env(svc, a, ssm.load_registry(), as_json)
        self.assertEqual(rc, 1)
        self.assertEqual(out.getvalue(), "")

    def test_quote_escaping(self):
        a, as_json = _env_args()
        svc = _FakeSvc([
            _fake_item("QUOTED", b"it's got 'quotes'", {}),
        ])
        with _capture_stdout() as out:
            rc = ssm.cmd_env(svc, a, ssm.load_registry(), as_json)
        self.assertEqual(rc, 0)
        self.assertEqual(out.getvalue(), "QUOTED='it'\\''s got '\\''quotes'\\'''\n")

    def test_nontext_secret_skipped(self):
        a, as_json = _env_args()
        svc = _FakeSvc([
            _fake_item("BINARY", b"\xff\xfe\x00secret", {}),
        ])
        with _capture_stdout() as out:
            rc = ssm.cmd_env(svc, a, ssm.load_registry(), as_json)
        self.assertEqual(rc, 1)
        self.assertEqual(out.getvalue(), "")

    def test_extra_attr_narrows(self):
        a, as_json = _env_args(app="kappa", attr=["scope=prod"])
        svc = _FakeSvc([
            _fake_item("A", b"1", {"service": "kappa", "scope": "prod"}),
            _fake_item("B", b"2", {"service": "kappa", "scope": "dev"}),
        ])
        with _capture_stdout() as out:
            rc = ssm.cmd_env(svc, a, ssm.load_registry(), as_json)
        text = out.getvalue()
        self.assertEqual(rc, 0)
        self.assertIn("A='1'", text)
        self.assertNotIn("B", text)


class TestAliasMap(unittest.TestCase):
    """Test the alias map loading and resolution."""

    def test_resolve_alias_identity(self):
        aliases = {}
        self.assertEqual(ssm._resolve_alias(aliases, "GITHUB_TOKEN"), ("GITHUB_TOKEN", False))

    def test_resolve_alias_map(self):
        aliases = {"GH_TOKEN": "GITHUB_TOKEN", "GITHUB_PAT": "GITHUB_TOKEN"}
        self.assertEqual(ssm._resolve_alias(aliases, "GH_TOKEN"), ("GITHUB_TOKEN", True))
        self.assertEqual(ssm._resolve_alias(aliases, "GITHUB_PAT"), ("GITHUB_TOKEN", True))
        self.assertEqual(ssm._resolve_alias(aliases, "GITHUB_TOKEN"), ("GITHUB_TOKEN", False))

    def test_simple_toml_load(self):
        import tempfile
        content = '[aliases]\nGH_TOKEN = "GITHUB_TOKEN"\nGITHUB_PAT = "GITHUB_TOKEN"\n'
        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode='w', suffix='.toml', delete=False) as f:
            f.write(content)
            tmp = f.name
        try:
            result = ssm._simple_toml_load(tmp)
            self.assertEqual(result, {"aliases": {"GH_TOKEN": "GITHUB_TOKEN", "GITHUB_PAT": "GITHUB_TOKEN"}})
        finally:
            os.unlink(tmp)

                rc = ssm.cmd_env(svc, a, ssm.load_registry(), False)
            self.assertEqual(rc, 0)
            text = out.getvalue()
            self.assertIn("GH_TOKEN=", text)
            self.assertIn("GITHUB_TOKEN=", text)
            self.assertIn("GITHUB_PAT=", text)
            self.assertIn("token123", text)
        finally:
            shutil.rmtree(td)

class _capture_stdout:
    """Context manager capturing writes to sys.stdout."""

    def __enter__(self):
        import io

        self._buf = io.StringIO()
        self._old = sys.stdout
        sys.stdout = self._buf
        return self._buf

    def __exit__(self, *exc):
        sys.stdout = self._old
        return False


class TestKeyringIntegration(unittest.TestCase):
    """Live D-Bus integration against the real (unlocked) login collection.
    Gated on SSM_TEST_KEYRING=1. Uses a uniquely-named item, deletes it after.
    Collection create/delete needs a GUI password prompt — covered only with
    SSM_TEST_COLLECTIONS=1 on an interactive session."""

    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        if os.environ.get("SSM_TEST_KEYRING") != "1":
            raise unittest.SkipTest("set SSM_TEST_KEYRING=1 to run live keyring tests")
        cls.svc = ssm.SecretService()
        cls.reg = ssm.load_registry()
        cls.coll = cls.svc.default_collection() or cls.svc.collections()[0]["path"]
        cls.test_id = "ssm-test-%d" % os.getpid()

    def test_set_get_search_delete(self):
        p = self.svc.set_item(self.coll, "secretsmith test item",
                              {"xdg:schema": "org.freedesktop.Secret.Generic",
                               "test-id": self.test_id},
                              b"s3cr3t-value", replace=True)
        self.assertTrue(p.startswith("/"))
        try:
            found = self.svc.search({"test-id": self.test_id})
            self.assertEqual(len(found), 1)
            self.assertEqual(found[0]["label"], "secretsmith test item")
            secret, _ct = self.svc.get_secret(found[0]["path"])
            self.assertEqual(secret, b"s3cr3t-value")
        finally:
            for it in self.svc.search({"test-id": self.test_id}):
                self.svc.delete_item(it["path"])
        self.assertEqual(self.svc.search({"test-id": self.test_id}), [])

    def test_chromium_entry_visible(self):
        schema, _ = ssm.resolve_schema("chromium", self.reg)
        found = self.svc.search({"xdg:schema": schema})
        self.assertTrue(found, "Chromium Safe Storage entry not found via registry")

    def test_collection_create_delete(self):
        if os.environ.get("SSM_TEST_COLLECTIONS") != "1":
            raise unittest.SkipTest("needs GUI keyring password prompt")
        name = "secretsmith-test-%d" % os.getpid()
        path = self.svc.create_collection(name)
        self.assertTrue(path.startswith("/"))
        self.svc.delete_collection(name)
